episodes.title: Astronaut float kyun karte hain?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 7 (g at height) + Ch 4 (free fall)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: variation of g with altitude, weightlessness in orbit
episodes.hook_text: Space mein gravity NAHI hoti? ❌
episodes.concept: Astronauts float because they are falling *with* their spaceship — not because gravity is missing.

episodes.title: Chaand har second Earth pe gir raha hai
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 7 (orbital motion, centripetal acceleration)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: orbital velocity, satellites
episodes.hook_text: Moon har second 1.4 mm GIRTA hai 🌙
episodes.concept: An orbit is falling so fast sideways that you keep missing the ground.

episodes.title: Escape Velocity: 11.2 km/s
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 7 (escape speed, v = √(2gR))
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: escape speed formula, why Moon has no atmosphere (classic NCERT exercise)
episodes.hook_text: Dilli → Mumbai in 2 MINUTE 🚀
episodes.concept: Escape velocity is the speed at which a thrown object never comes back — and it explains why the Moon has no air.

episodes.title: January mein Earth Sun ke sabse PAAS hoti hai
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 7 (Kepler's laws — 2nd law)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: Kepler's 2nd law, areal velocity, ellipse orbits
episodes.hook_text: January = Earth Sun ke SABSE PAAS. Phir thand kyun? ❄️
episodes.concept: Seasons come from Earth's tilt, not distance — and Earth speeds up when it's closest to the Sun (Kepler's 2nd law).

episodes.title: Bhaari cheez pehle girti hai?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 2 (free fall, g independent of mass)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: free fall, why a = g for all masses
episodes.hook_text: Bowling ball vs Tennis ball — kaun pehle? 🎳🎾
episodes.concept: Gravity pulls heavy things harder, but heavy things are equally harder to move — so everything falls with the same acceleration.

episodes.title: Goli chalao ya giraao — dono SAATH girti hain
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 3 (projectile motion — independence of horizontal & vertical motion)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: projectile time of flight
episodes.hook_text: Fired bullet vs dropped bullet 🔫 — kaun pehle?
episodes.concept: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent; gravity doesn't care how fast you move sideways.

episodes.title: Earth 1,07,000 km/h se bhaag rahi hai. Feel kyun nahi hota?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (Newton's 1st law, inertia, Galileo)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: inertial frames, first law
episodes.hook_text: Tum abhi 1,07,000 km/h se ja rahe ho 🌍💨
episodes.concept: You only feel *changes* in speed — constant motion is invisible (Newton's first law).

episodes.title: Tumhara weight 60 kg NAHI hai
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (mass vs weight, W = mg, apparent weight in a lift)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: lift problems, weightlessness
episodes.hook_text: Tumhara weight 60 kg? ❌ WRONG
episodes.concept: Mass is how much stuff you are (kg); weight is the force Earth pulls you with (newton) — and a weighing machine measures force.

episodes.title: Ghoda gaadi kheenchta hai, gaadi ghode ko. Toh gaadi CHALTI kaise hai?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (Newton's 3rd law — action & reaction act on different bodies)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE: the classic paradox, asked in some form every year
episodes.hook_text: Newton ka 3rd law kehta hai gaadi CHAL hi nahi sakti?! 🐎
episodes.concept: Action–reaction pairs never cancel because they act on two different bodies; the cart moves because of the ground's push on the horse.

episodes.title: Truck vs Car: force kis par zyada?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (3rd law + a = F/m)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: equal forces, unequal accelerations
episodes.hook_text: Truck 🚛 vs Car 🚗 — force kis par ZYADA?
episodes.concept: In any collision both bodies feel exactly equal force; the damage difference comes from acceleration = F/m.

episodes.title: Catch lete waqt haath PEECHE kyun kheenchte hain?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (impulse, F·Δt = Δp — the cricket example is literally in the NCERT text)
episodes.exam_focus: NEET/Boards: impulse-momentum, airbags
episodes.hook_text: Fielder haath peeche kyun kheenchta hai? 🏏 Style nahi, physics
episodes.concept: The change in momentum is fixed; spreading it over more time means less force — impulse.

episodes.title: Friction na hoti... toh tum ek kadam nahi chal paate
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (friction — static is self-adjusting, walking)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: static vs kinetic friction, f ≤ μN
episodes.hook_text: Friction DUSHMAN hai? Ek kadam chalo bina friction 👣
episodes.concept: Friction is what pushes you forward when you walk — and static friction is smart: it is only as large as needed.

episodes.title: Centrifugal force EXIST nahi karta
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 & 5 (uniform circular motion, centripetal force)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE: pseudo forces, banking of roads; NEET: centripetal force
episodes.hook_text: Gaadi mudti hai, tum bahar 'phenke' jaate ho — yeh force JHOOTH hai 🚗
episodes.concept: Nothing throws you outward; you keep going straight while the car turns under you. The only real force is inward — centripetal.

episodes.title: 1 ghanta deewar dhakela... kaam ZERO
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 5 (work W = F·d·cosθ)
episodes.exam_focus: Boards/NEET: zero-work cases — the most-asked 1-marker of the chapter
episodes.hook_text: 1 ghanta deewar dhakela. Physics: 'Kaam ZERO' 😭
episodes.concept: In physics, work needs force AND displacement in the direction of the force — otherwise it is zero, no matter how tired you are.

episodes.title: Tum ek 100 WATT ka bulb ho
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 5 (power P = W/t, watt, kilowatt-hour)
episodes.exam_focus: Boards: "1 unit = 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J" — guaranteed question
episodes.hook_text: Tum = 100 W bulb 💡 (aur bijli ka 'unit' kya hai?)
episodes.concept: Power is energy per second; a "unit" on your electricity bill is energy (1 kWh = 3.6 million joules), not power.

episodes.title: Energy kabhi khatam NAHI hoti... toh "Energy Crisis" kya hai?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 5 (conservation of energy) → seeds Ch 11 Thermodynamics (2nd law, entropy)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: energy conservation, dissipative forces
episodes.hook_text: Energy kabhi khatam nahi hoti. Toh 'Energy Crisis' kya bakwaas hai? ⚡
episodes.concept: Energy is never destroyed — it spreads out as heat and becomes useless. Energy crisis = useful-energy crisis.

episodes.title: Space mein kuch nahi hai... toh rocket kis cheez ko push karta hai?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 4 (conservation of linear momentum, rocket propulsion)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: momentum conservation, recoil
episodes.hook_text: Space khaali hai. Rocket kis cheez ko PUSH karta hai? 🚀
episodes.concept: A rocket pushes nothing — it throws its own mass backward, and momentum conservation carries it forward.

episodes.title: Darwaze ka handle KINAARE pe kyun hota hai?
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 6 (torque τ = r × F, moment arm)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: torque, lever, equilibrium
episodes.hook_text: Darwaze ka handle beech mein kyun nahi hota? 🚪
episodes.concept: Turning needs torque = force × distance from the pivot; more distance, less effort.

episodes.title: Ek earthquake ne DIN chhota kar diya
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 6 (conservation of angular momentum, L = Iω)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: skater problem, moment of inertia
episodes.hook_text: 2011 earthquake ne din 1.8 microsecond CHHOTA kar diya ⏰
episodes.concept: Angular momentum (mass-spread × spin) is conserved: pull mass inward and spin speeds up — for skaters and for planets.

episodes.title: Yeh challenge KOI nahi kar sakta (Season finale)
episodes.ncert_chapter: NCERT XI Ch 6 (centre of mass, balance/toppling)
episodes.exam_focus: JEE/NEET: centre of mass, stability
episodes.hook_text: Yeh challenge koi nahi kar sakta. ABHI try karo 🧱
episodes.concept: You stay balanced only while your centre of mass is above your supporting foot — the wall stops you from shifting it.
